cheese-spread-american-or-cheddar-cheese.title: Cheese spread, American or Cheddar cheese base, reduced fat

content.title: About
content.content: Cheese spread made from American or Cheddar cheese with reduced fat is a smooth, easily spreadable paste with a characteristic creamy flavor. It contains less fat than traditional cheese spreads while retaining a rich cheese taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese spread is often used as a base for sandwiches, appetizers, and sauces.
Reduced fat is achieved by partially replacing butter with low‑fat dairy ingredients.
American and Cheddar cheeses have a milder flavor compared to many European cheeses, making the spread versatile.
The product is frequently fortified with calcium and vitamin D to support bone health.
Cheese spread can be used to create creamy sauces without adding extra fat.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Cheese spread provides a notable amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The cheese base supplies high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Reduced fat content
items.content: Compared with regular spreads, the lower fat level makes it more suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamins B2 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotics (when added)
items.content: Some versions are enriched with probiotic cultures that help maintain gut flora.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy proteins or lactose may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain varieties may contain higher salt levels, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: To extend shelf life, preservatives may be added, which some consumers prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread cheese spread on bread, crackers, vegetable sticks, use as a filling for rolls, in pasta sauces, or in casseroles. It can be mixed with herbs, spices, or yogurt to create new flavor profiles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2 °C–6 °C in the original packaging. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors, color changes, or mold.

content.title: About
content.content: The McDonalds Hamburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a grilled beef patty, bun, slice of cheese, pickles, onions and a special sauce. It originated in the 1940s in the United States and has become one of the most recognizable dishes of the chain.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first McDonalds hamburger was sold in 1948 at the brothers' restaurant in California.
Since 1975 the menu has featured the signature "Special Sauce", a closely guarded recipe.
McDonalds sells over 75 million hamburgers worldwide each year.
Ingredient composition varies by country; for example, India uses a chicken patty instead of beef.
The hamburger is frequently highlighted in promotional campaigns, including limited‑edition sauces.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The burger contains vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: Its high calorie content provides a quick energy boost, useful during periods of increased physical activity.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Frequent consumption can contribute to weight gain and elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt in the bun and sauce raises sodium intake, which may affect blood pressure.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Contains milk, gluten, and sometimes soy, making it a potential allergen.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some regions include preservatives that may cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The hamburger is typically eaten by hand, holding the bottom bun. It can be paired with fries, sauce, and a drink. For a healthier option, replace the beef patty with chicken or a plant‑based alternative.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Freshly prepared burgers should be consumed immediately. Leftovers can be stored in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, then reheated to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

infant-formula-store-brand-gentle-or-sen.title: Infant Formula, Store Brand, Gentle or Sensitivity

content.title: About
content.content: The “Gentle” (or “Sensitivity”) infant formula is a nutritionally complete milk substitute designed for newborns and infants with heightened sensitivity to standard formulas. It features easily digestible proteins, minimal allergens, and is fortified with vitamins, minerals, and DHA to support growth and brain development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Manufactured under ISO 9001 and GMP quality standards.
Contains prebiotics to promote a healthy gut microbiome.
Free of gluten, soy protein, and lactose, making it suitable for children with intolerances.
Packaged in recyclable material; the company runs programs to reduce food waste.
Clinically tested to confirm its hypoallergenic properties.

items.title: Supports Growth
items.content: A balanced ratio of protein, fat, and carbohydrates provides the energy and building blocks needed for healthy physical development.

items.title: Brain Development
items.content: DHA and ARA support the development of the visual and nervous systems in infants.

items.title: Digestive Health
items.content: Prebiotics and easily digestible proteins help reduce the risk of constipation and intestinal irritation.

items.title: Immune Support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, E and zinc strengthen the immune system during this critical period.

items.title: Hypoallergenic
items.content: Absence of common allergens (soy, gluten, lactose) lowers the chance of allergic reactions.

items.title: Milk Protein Allergy
items.content: Despite its hypoallergenic design, some infants may still react to casein.

items.title: Improper Reconstitution
items.content: A solution that is too concentrated can strain the kidneys; always follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

items.title: Shelf Life After Opening
items.content: Prepared formula should be used within 48 hours and kept refrigerated.

items.title: Temperature Control
items.content: Feeding with milk that is too hot or too cold can irritate the baby’s stomach.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix the formula with clean, boiled water, cool to body temperature (≈37 °C), and feed the baby according to pediatric guidance. It can also be added to prepared infant cereals if needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and use within 48 hours. Discard if the product develops an off‑smell, color, or taste.
